event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: YUM’s 2021-02-22 Form 10-K portrays COVID-19 as a severe, multi-faceted, still-unfolding threat that is materially affecting every layer of the company’s global restaurant system.  The filing makes clear that the pandemic is not merely a hypothetical future concern but an event that has already reduced revenues, forced permanent store closures, caused goodwill and asset impairments, raised operating costs (PPE, cleaning, labour premiums), interrupted supplies, and driven franchisees into financial distress.  Management repeatedly states that these pressures will “continue,” underscoring that the risk horizon extends well beyond the 2020 financial year.  The disclosures are specific—naming lost revenues, dine-in bans, labour shortages, and potential liquidity strain—rather than boiler-plate, and they establish direct causal links to COVID-19.  Because the filing date is within one year of the World Health Organization’s pandemic declaration (March 2020), the Time Decay Principle permits high severity scores (7-10).  I therefore weight sentences that show realised, quantified, or system-wide impacts most heavily, while forward-looking or partially mitigated statements receive moderate scores.  Sentences that describe upside (e.g., drive-thru sales gains) are treated as mitigating factors and scored lower.  Collectively, the evidence supports an overall risk level near the top of the scale for a recent event with ongoing, material consequences.

evidence_list.snippet: The novel coronavirus (COVID-19) global pandemic has had, and is expected to continue to have, an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links COVID-19 to actual adverse effects already incurred.
Projects continued future adverse effects, signalling sustained risk.
Applies to overall business and results, indicating enterprise-wide materiality.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct statement of realised and continuing enterprise-wide harm justifies a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: Developments related to COVID-19 have had and are expected to continue to have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Confirms past adverse impacts.
Emphasises future continuation of those impacts.
Covers the whole business and financial results.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Very similar to snippet 1 but slightly less forceful wording; scored 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The impacts of COVID-19 have included the ongoing loss of revenues due to reduced and limited store-level operations, continued or increased full or partial dining room closures, other restrictions on our business and operations, continued delays in reopening, and an increase in the number of permanent restaurant closures during the year ended December 31, 2020.

components.reason: Lists multiple concrete operational and financial harms (revenue loss, closures).
Describes impacts as ‘ongoing,’ highlighting persistence.
Quantifies timing (during 2020) showing realised effect.
Mentions permanent restaurant closures, signalling long-term structural damage.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed enumeration of realised, structural damages warrants a 9.

evidence_list.snippet: Additionally, we and our franchisees have made operational changes intended to safeguard employees and customers in response to COVID-19, including increased cleaning and sanitization, installation of counter 9 screens and purchasing personal protective equipment, which have increased and may continue to increase restaurant operating costs and impact restaurant-level margins and return on invested capital.

components.reason: Specifies cost-increasing mitigation measures (PPE, cleaning).
States these measures already ‘have increased’ costs— realised impact.
Acknowledges future cost pressure (‘may continue’).
Links to financial metrics (margins, ROIC).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete cost pressures tied to key profitability metrics earn a solid 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Our and our franchisees restaurants may experience interruptions of food and other supplies as well as labor shortages as a result of COVID-19, thereby disrupting our and our franchisees operations and impacting same-store sales negatively.

components.reason: Identifies supply chain disruptions and labour shortages linked to pandemic.
Connects disruptions to negative sales impact (same-store sales).
Covers both company-owned and franchise operations, broad scope.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct tie of COVID-19 to supply chain, labour and sales risk scores 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Our success is heavily reliant on our Concepts’ franchisees, and the COVID-19 pandemic has caused and may continue to cause financial distress for certain franchisees, particularly those located in areas most significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Links pandemic to franchisee financial distress, a core dependency.
Notes both realised (‘has caused’) and future (‘may continue’) effects.
Highlights geographic concentration of impact (areas most affected).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Franchisee solvency risk is significant but less quantified, earning 6.

evidence_list.snippet: We are unable to fully predict the impact that COVID-19 will have on our and our franchisees’ operations going forward due to various uncertainties, including the severity and duration of the outbreak, the timing and availability of effective medical treatments and vaccines, the timing and effectiveness of the ongoing rollout of vaccines, the extent to which COVID-19 may cause customers to continue to be reluctant to return to in-restaurant dining or otherwise change their consumption patterns (including after the COVID-19 pandemic has ended), additional actions that may be taken by governmental authorities, and the length and severity of ongoing negative economic conditions in the U.S. and globally arising from the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple uncertainty drivers (vaccines, consumer behaviour, government actions).
Acknowledges inability to predict, signalling high risk volatility.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Focus on uncertainty rather than quantified loss yields a mid-level 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Moreover, if conditions related to the COVID-19 pandemic result in significant disruptions to capital and financial markets, or negatively impact our credit ratings, our cost of borrowing, our ability to access capital on favorable terms and our overall liquidity and capital structure could be adversely impacted.

components.reason: Highlights potential funding and liquidity risks tied to pandemic market disruptions.
Specifies multiple financial channels (borrowing costs, credit ratings).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking but serious capital-market exposure merits a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Finally, the negative economic conditions arising from the COVID-19 pandemic have resulted in the impairment of the value of certain of our restaurant assets as well as the goodwill impairment charge we incurred with respect to our Habit Burger Grill reporting unit in the first quarter of 2020.

components.reason: Reports an actual asset and goodwill impairment directly caused by pandemic.
Quantifies impact category (asset value, goodwill), indicating material accounting effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realised balance-sheet damage lifts severity to 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Conversely, for our restaurants that prominently feature drive-thru, carryout and delivery options, COVID-19 has in many cases contributed to an increase in sales during 2020.

components.reason: Acknowledges pandemic-driven upside, a mitigating factor.
Still ties performance variability directly to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes beneficial effect; treated as mitigation, therefore negative score.

evidence_list.snippet: If the impact of COVID-19 recedes, in-person dining restrictions are lifted or lessened and the restaurant industry in general returns to more normal operations, the benefits to sales experienced by certain of our restaurants, including our Pizza Hut delivery restaurants, could wane and our results could be negatively impacted.

components.reason: Flags risk of sales decline once pandemic tailwinds fade.
Highlights dependence on temporary pandemic-era channel mix.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Moderate forward risk of post-pandemic reversal earns 4.

evidence_list.snippet: We may not achieve our target development goals, including as the result of the COVID-19 pandemic, and new restaurants may not be profitable.

components.reason: Links pandemic to slowed unit development and profitability risks.
Potentially hampers long-term growth strategy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Growth-strategy risk is important but less immediately quantified, so 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Future shortages or disruptions could be caused by inclement weather, natural disasters, pandemics (including the COVID-19 pandemic), inaccurate forecasting of customer demand, problems in production or distribution, restrictions on imports or exports including due to trade disputes or restrictions, the inability of vendors to obtain credit, political instability in the countries in which the suppliers and distributors are located, the financial instability of suppliers and distributors, suppliers’ or distributors’ failure to meet our standards or requirements, transitioning to new suppliers or distributors, product quality issues, inflation, other factors relating to the suppliers and distributors and the countries in which they are located, food safety warnings or advisories or the prospect of such pronouncements, product recalls, the cancellation of supply or distribution agreements or an inability to renew such arrangements or to find replacements on commercially reasonable terms, or other conditions beyond our control or the control of our Concepts’ franchisees.

components.reason: Explicitly lists pandemics including COVID-19 as a supply-chain disruption source.
Enumerates wide operational impacts from such disruptions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic supply-chain wording with COVID-19 reference scores a modest 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Our and our Concepts’ franchisees may experience a shortage of labor for positions in our restaurants, including due to concern over exposure to COVID-19 and other factors that could decrease the pool of available qualified employees for key functions.

components.reason: Connects labour shortages specifically to COVID-19 health concerns.
Implies operational disruption across company and franchise network.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pandemic-driven labour risk impacts operations; rated 5.
